P001.text: Act on the sampled orders and the documentary traces linking approval decisions, order placement and purchasing-system records.

P002.text: The historical approval process is not directly observable; reconstruct it through multiple record paths.

P003.text: The packet establishes that 14 of 90 sampled orders lack purchasing-system approval attachments, but does not establish that approval was absent.

P004.text: Verify which orders exceeded the threshold and what the internal rule required at the time.

P005.text: Assume only provisionally that records can be linked and their dates interpreted reliably.

P006.text: During week one, build a candidate model of how documented approval should precede an order and reach the purchasing record, including any permitted routes through meeting minutes or delegated-authority forms.

P007.text: For each of the 14 flagged orders, trace paths from the purported approval through relevant records to order placement and attachment.

P008.text: Use the other sampled orders to test whether these routes also explain apparently complete records.

P009.text: Record order identifiers, amounts, approval content, applicable authority, event dates, record-creation dates and attachment dates, distinguishing these dates explicitly.

P010.text: A delegation form may establish authority without documenting approval of a particular order.

P011.text: During week two, compare observed links, timing and missing traces with each route's predictions.

P012.text: Investigate discrepancies through targeted record requests and staff clarification; treat recollections as leads rather than equivalent to contemporaneous documentation.

P013.text: Iteratively revise the candidate account and check its predictions against additional traces.

P014.text: Track alternative explanations rather than adjusting the account merely to make every order appear compliant.

P015.text: Observe whether predicted approval records can be found, linked to the relevant order and shown to precede placement, and whether their recorded authority fits the applicable rule.

P016.text: The counterpart to propagation behavior is the timing and continuity of documentary traces across approval-to-order-to-system paths.

P017.text: Look for structured discrepancies by approval route, responsible role, period or record location: for example, linked prior approvals without attachments, attachments without demonstrated prior approval, or repeated breaks at a particular handoff.

P018.text: These are proposed observations to test, not findings.

P019.text: Record searches that yield no result together with their scope and access limitations.

P020.text: Use the pattern of discrepancies to constrain competing accounts of where the process departed from its predicted route: obtaining approval, documenting it, linking it to an order, or attaching it to the system.

P021.text: Reliable evidence of appropriately authorized, documented approval before placement can support satisfaction of the given approval rule even when an attachment is missing, subject to the rule's actual record requirements.

P022.text: An attachment alone does not establish timely approval.

P023.text: An unsuccessful search supports 'approval not located within the searched sources,' not automatically 'approval never occurred.' Seek further records that distinguish competing accounts.

P024.text: Before the board review in week three, prepare an order-level evidence table separating supported conclusions, unresolved cases and alternative explanations; propose record corrections or process changes tied to the supported failure points.

P025.text: Record paths may be sparse, uneven, dependent on copied material or affected by missing records, ambiguous identifiers, unreliable timestamps and uncertain approval origins.

P026.text: Standardizing all orders into one assumed workflow could conceal legitimate routes or manufacture apparent failures; retain exceptions and test assumptions.

P027.text: Multiple historical processes may produce the same surviving records.

P028.text: Do not infer a population failure rate from 14 of 90 without a defensible sampling basis, and do not make legal conclusions.

P029.text: Stop an individual inquiry when sufficient reliable evidence resolves the applicable rule or when identified sources are exhausted and the remaining uncertainty is documented.

P030.text: At the board deadline, report unresolved cases without forcing closure, assigning each a specific next evidence request and responsible owner.

P031.text: Preserve original records when adding links or annotations; any later approval or remediation must retain its actual date and must not be presented as prior approval.
